articles.headline: QB Baker Mayfield says Bucs need to 'fight our way out' of 0-2 start
articles.description: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield admitted to being "pretty shocked" the Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since he has been their quarterback and the first time since 2014 after losing to his former team, the Browns, 23-19.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield admitted to being "pretty shocked" the Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since he has been their quarterback and the first time since 2014 after losing to his former team, the Cleveland Browns, 23-19.

"Pretty shocked. But it's where we're at. So we've got to fight our way out," said Mayfield, who could not lead the Bucs back from a 23-19 deficit against the team that selected him first overall in the 2018 NFL draft and traded him away in 2022.

Mayfield is now 0-2 against the Browns with his previous loss coming as a member of the Carolina Panthers, to whom the Browns traded him after securing quarterback Deshaun Watson in a deal with the Houston Texans.

Mayfield told the "Fourth & South Podcast" earlier this summer that he had this game circled on the calendar since the schedule came out. When asked if this loss stings more given the circumstances, he said, "No, [it] just stings more because we're 0-2."

"It's shooting ourselves in the foot, not making the plays when we need them, knowing that these are fixable things, but that also makes it more frustrating," Mayfield said. "But just got to get it corrected. We've got to be harder on ourselves, watch the tape, get those things fixed, flush it and move it on to the next."

The Browns grabbed the lead with 3:57 to go in regulation on a 17-yard touchdown pass from Watson to Blake Whiteheart that, with the PAT attempt, made it 23-19. A lightning delay right at the two-minute mark sent both teams into the locker room for two hours and 12 minutes.

When play resumed, running back Bucky Irving converted a third-and-1 with a 6-yard run that brought the Bucs down to the Cleveland 13-yard line. But a holding penalty on center Graham Barton on the very next play forced the Bucs into a second-and-14 situation from the Browns' 23.

On that play, Mayfield found rookie Ted Hurst III one-on-one on a go route against Mekhi Blackmon along the left sideline. Hurst, a third-round draft pick out of Georgia State who saw more targets than any other Bucs receiver Sunday and was brought in to help replace longtime X wide receiver Mike Evans, couldn't hang on to the ball as he slid into the end zone.

Hurst said rain wasn't a factor despite a heavy downpour that had visibly saturated the field and the ball. Still, those are conditions the Bucs have simulated in practice, including this week, with anticipation of inclement weather.

"No, honestly, I just have to make that play," Hurst said, adding that he thought he was going to score on the play.

After a 3-yard scramble from Mayfield, his last-gasp effort came on a fourth-and-11 throw to Emeka Egbuka, with whom Mayfield connected earlier on a 5-yard score. This time, however, Mayfield overthrew the second-year wideout.

articles.headline: Nashville turf temps of 157 F melt cleats, send Sirianni for IV
articles.description: Players cleats were melting and head coach Nick Sirianni needed an IV as a result of extreme heat conditions at Nissan Stadium during Sunday's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, a 24-20 Eagles win.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Players' cleats were melting and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni needed an IV as a result of extreme heat conditions at Nissan Stadium during Sunday's game between Philadelphia and the Tennessee Titans, a 24-20 win for the Eagles.

The temperature on the turf reached 157 degrees Fahrenheit, per the television broadcast.

Philadelphia left tackle Jordan Mailata, the team's NFL Players Association rep in 2025, said this is another reason why the union should push for the league to do away with turf surfaces.

"I've never thought about how hot a stadium can be if it's turf. [The heat] just sits there and bounces up into you," Mailata said. "We've got to bring it up. This is why we want all grass fields, to create a standard of play in the league where we're not putting players in dangerous positions if we don't have to."

Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens noted postgame that his feet were "burning, still hurting." Jurgens said he went through multiple pairs of cleats due to melting issues.

"Halftime was like a NASCAR pit crew helping me get ready for the second half," he said. "That turf was just radiating."

The temperature in Nashville for Sunday's kickoff of noon local time was 95 degrees, with a heat index of around 105. A "heat dome" had settled over the area in recent weeks, with high pressure in the atmosphere pushing heat toward the surface and trapping it there.

Titans safety Amani Hooker said the midsoles of his cleats "melted completely off" in the season opener against the visiting New York Jets.

Mailata said he rolled his ankles twice in the game and wondered if it could be the result of his shoes bending because the plastic in the bottom of his cleats got soft.

Television cameras showed a member of the Titans having his cleats sprayed with water to cool them off.

"It was hot as s---," Sirianni said. "I didn't play a snap and I had to get an IV. I so appreciate how much the guys prepared. I so appreciate how much they fought through because it wasn't easy."

There was some conversation after the game centered around the idea that teams would not be permitted to practice outdoors in such conditions, making it curious why the league continues to schedule early afternoon September games in hot-weather climates.

The Eagles played in similar conditions each of the past two seasons at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Safety Reed Blankenship had to exit the Bucs game in 2024 with a heat-related illness that was considered serious at the time.

The Eagles left for Nashville on Friday, a day earlier than normal, to try to acclimate to the heat. They held a midday walk-through Saturday to try to get players used to the conditions.

"It was one of the top five toughest games I've been a part of," said Philadelphia tackle Lane Johnson, a 14-year veteran. "It was a mental test for everyone involved."

articles.headline: Brock Purdy keeps 49ers rolling with 'MVP' game vs. Dolphins
articles.description: Brock Purdy authored a near-perfect game at quarterback in the 49ers' 35-13 win over the rebuilding Dolphins, ending the day with a 99.7 QBR.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- As San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy wrapped up his media availability after Sunday's win against the Miami Dolphins, linebacker Fred Warner greeted Purdy, pointed to him and declared "MVP."

Just two weeks into the season, it's far too early for any sweeping award declarations, but Purdy's performance against the rebuilding Dolphins on Sunday was so close to perfect that Warner wanted the world to know he sees where Purdy could go in his fifth NFL season.

"Brock is unbelievable," Warner said. "I've spoken on how great of a preseason he had and his camp, his command of the offense, but it's different. We get judged on those three hours that we're out there. For him to be operating the offense the way he is right now, it doesn't matter who the other pieces are. As long as Brock's the one that's being the point guard, I know we're good."

After a weeklong stay in Melbourne, Australia, to open the season, there were plenty of questions this week about whether the Niners might have a letdown against a Dolphins team that is in the first year of a roster teardown.

Purdy heard that chatter and silenced it with one of his best and most complete games as the Niners rolled to a 35-13 win to improve to 2-0. Combined with their 27-7 win against the Los Angeles Rams last week, San Francisco has started the season with back-to-back wins of 20-plus points to open a season for the first time in franchise history.

With Purdy at the controls, the Niners scored a touchdown on each of their first five possessions, the first time they've done that in the past 45 seasons, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

After receiver Deebo Samuel dropped Purdy's third pass attempt, Purdy rattled off 18 straight completions, a streak that ended only when officials flagged him for intentional grounding on his final pass of the day.

Purdy said he wasn't even aware of the streak as he was too busy trying to help push the Niners to a bigger lead after getting just two offensive possessions in the first half.

"I honestly didn't know until towards the end, fourth quarter maybe," Purdy said. "For me, every play, every drive mattered. It wasn't like we went out there and just blew these guys out. It was a game. And that's what we're saying. That's the NFL. That's where my headspace was at."

By the time it was over, Purdy was 20-of-22 for 287 yards with two touchdowns for a 99.7 QBR and tacked on 30 rushing yards with another score. In the process, he became the second player in NFL history with 250-plus passing yards with a completion rate of 90% or better in multiple games, joining Derek Carr at that mark.

Purdy also is the first quarterback in league history to hit both those marks in a game with 30 or more rushing yards. Entering the Sunday night game, Purdy leads the league in QBR (95.9) and completion percentage (80.4%) and is tied for fifth in touchdown passes (five).

articles.headline: Kirk Cousins' 'phenomenal' play has new-look Raiders at 2-0
articles.description: Kirk Cousins has done more than just help the Raiders transition through a rebuilding process after two games, leading Las Vegas to their first 2-0 record since 2021.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Kirk Cousins became the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback to help jumpstart the rebuild process under first-time head coach Klint Kubiak.

His presence has paid dividends thus far.

Cousins threw for 253 yards, three touchdowns and an interception to lead the Raiders past the Chargers, 26-14, on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium, improving to 2-0 for the first time since 2021.

Cousins had a 65.5% completion rate and posted a passer rating of 113.1. It was a performance that had wide receiver Tre Tucker clamoring about Cousins postgame, saying the 38-year-old signal caller "can probably play until he is 60."

 

"It's still early, but the goal is to build something that way outlasts me," said Cousins, who has thrown six touchdowns in two games. He is the second player in team history to record six touchdown passes in the first two games, joining former quarterback Ken Stabler in 1976.

Cousins proved that in Year 15, he still has a bit of arm strength. A week after he completed 1 of 7 pass attempts for 21 yards and two interceptions on throws for 10-plus air yards, he was effective on those throws. On attempts of 10-plus air yards, Cousins completed 8 of 12 passes for 181 yards, three touchdowns and an interception.

Cousins' interception with 9:05 to go in the first quarter was a result of Tucker slipping while running his route, which led to cornerback Cam Hart catching the ball. Cousins, however, had a nice response in the second quarter. With 12 minutes to go, Cousins completed a 40-yard touchdown pass to Tucker to give the Raiders a 7-0 lead.

During the final seconds of the quarter, Cousins found Tucker again for a 42-yard completion that set up a 59-yard field goal attempt from kicker Matt Gay to give Las Vegas a 10-7 lead at halftime. Tucker finished with five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

"[Cousins] did a really good job of pushing the ball down the field," Kubiak said. "Our playmakers, like Tre, made some really big plays. It's something you're always trying to do every weekend."

Trailing by four points in the third quarter, Cousins helped the Raiders score 17 unanswered points to secure the victory. He engineered the comeback, starting with a 27-yard pass to wide receiver Dareke Young. Cousins tossed the ball to running back Ashton Jeanty, who threw it back to him before he found Young open down the field while a defender was closing in.

Three plays later, Cousins threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Cody White. In the fourth quarter, both players connected for an 11-yard touchdown, which gave Las Vegas a 13-point advantage.

"He's elite, man. I'm so excited to play with him," Tucker said. "He does not look any bit old to me, and the things I see him doing in practice, he's doing in the games."

Kubiak said: "He's been phenomenal with the operations and leadership. I can't say enough great things about No. 8."

articles.headline: 2026 MLB ABS challenge system tracker: Team, player rankings
articles.description: The ABS challenge system leaderboard ranks batters, catchers, teams and umpires throughout the MLB season.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball implemented the ABS challenge system for the 2026 season, which allows players to challenge a ball or strike call made by the plate umpire. Each team receives two challenges to start the game, and only batters, pitchers and catchers can challenge a call. If a team wins a challenge, it can keep challenging. If a team challenges incorrectly twice, it loses its challenges for the rest of the game.

articles.headline: Brewers set franchise record with 98th victory, beat Orioles 3-0 to complete sweep
articles.description: — William Contreras homered, and the Milwaukee Brewers earned their franchise-record 98th victory by beating the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 on Sunday night to complete a three-game sweep.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — William Contreras homered, and the Milwaukee Brewers earned their franchise-record 98th victory by beating the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 on Sunday night to complete a three-game sweep.


              Cooper Pratt drove in two for Milwaukee (98-58), which owns the best record in the majors and surpassed the 97 victories it had last season. The Brewers have already clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title.


              The Orioles managed four hits and were shut out for the second consecutive game. Baltimore fell five games behind the Chicago White Sox for the AL’s third wild card and has six games remaining.


              Milwaukee starter Jacob Misiorowski yielded a hit and struck out four in three innings in a planned abbreviated outing. The right-hander, who leads the majors in ERA (1.86) and strikeouts (247), moved into second place on the Brewers’ single-season strikeouts list. Ben Sheets had 264 in 2004.


              The Brewers manufactured a run in the second inning against Baltimore starter Brandon Young (9-5) when Jake Bauers walked, advanced on a grounder and scored on Pratt’s two-out single to left.


              Contreras smacked Young’s sinker 403 feet to left to lead off the fourth for his 18th homer.


              Pratt added an RBI single in the seventh against Orioles reliever Félix Bautista, who completed his comeback from shoulder surgery. He had not pitched in the majors since July 20, 2025.


              DL Hall (4-0) pitched 1 2/3 innings for Milwaukee. Trevor Megill worked the ninth for his 29th save.


              The Brewers’ Jackson Chourio stole two bases to give him 21 for the year. He joined Seattle’s Julio Rodríguez and Kansas City’s Bobby Witt Jr. as the only players with 20 homers and 20 steals in three consecutive seasons to open a career.


              Young allowed two runs and struck out a career-high nine in six innings.


              Up next
              Milwaukee is off Monday. RHP Dustin May (7-9, 4.61 ERA) faces Philadelphia as the Brewers open their last road series Tuesday. Baltimore’s final homestand continues Monday as RHP Shane Baz (6-5, 4.11 ERA) starts against Toronto.
